record.original_question: For random point configurations on the sphere, such as uniform i.i.d. samples or points from a determinantal point process, can one quantify how good the points are by studying the integration weights of the associated spherical interpolation scheme—specifically, by measuring positivity of the weights or how close they are to 1/N?

evidence.quote: Question 6.1 (Jordi Marzo). Consider random points on the sphere (uniform i.i.d or from a determinantal point process). Can one quantify how good the points are using the notion of positivity of the integration weights (or being close to 1/N)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{S}^d \subset \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ denote the unit sphere equipped with its normalized surface measure $\sigma$. For an integer $N$, let $X_N = \{x_1,\dots,x_N\} \subset \mathbb{S}^d$ be a random point configuration drawn according to one of the following models:
(a) the points $x_i$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $\mathbb{S}^d$ with respect to $\sigma$;
(b) the points $x_i$ form a determinantal point process on $\mathbb{S}^d$ (for instance the harmonic ensemble of degree $L$ where $N$ equals the dimension of the space of spherical polynomials of degree $\le L$).

Fix a finite-dimensional space $\mathcal{P}_L$ of spherical polynomials of degree $\le L$ on $\mathbb{S}^d$ such that $\dim \mathcal{P}_L = N$, and assume that with positive probability $X_N$ is unisolvent for $\mathcal{P}_L$. The associated interpolatory cubature rule assigns weights $w_1,\dots,w_N \in \mathbb{R}$ characterized by
$$\int_{\mathbb{S}^d} p\,\mathrm{d}\sigma \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^N w_i\, p(x_i) \qquad \text{for all } p \in \mathcal{P}_L.$$

The point set $X_N$ is regarded as "good" for numerical integration when these weights are all positive and close to the equal-weight value $1/N$.

Quantify the quality of such random point configurations by establishing precise probabilistic estimates on the integration weights $w_i$. Specifically, determine asymptotic or non-asymptotic bounds (as $N \to \infty$) for:
(i) the probability that all weights $w_i$ are positive;
(ii) deviation quantities such as $\max_i |w_i - 1/N|$, $\sum_i (w_i - 1/N)^2$, or $\min_i w_i$,
under each of the two random models above.
artifact.category_tag: spherical cubature and determinantal point processes
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search reveals related work on determinantal point processes on the sphere (harmonic ensemble, spherical ensemble) and on QMC designs, including studies by Beltrán, Marzo, and Ortega-Cerdà on Riesz energy, and recent work on linear statistics and pair correlations of DPPs on spheres. However, no source was found that specifically quantifies the positivity of interpolation weights or their closeness to 1/N for random (i.i.d. or DPP) sphere configurations. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Linear statistics of determinantal point processes and norm representations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies linear statistics of DPPs related to sphere integration but does not address interpolation weight positivity.
status_evidence.claim: Related DPP-on-sphere research exists but does not resolve the weight-positivity question.

status_evidence.title: QMC Designs and Determinantal Point Processes
status_evidence.snippet: DPPs are studied as equal-weight QMC rules on the sphere, focusing on worst-case integration error in Sobolev spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Existing DPP/QMC literature treats equal-weight rules and integration error, not interpolatory weight quality.

status_evidence.title: Extremal Systems of Points and Numerical Integration on the Sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Extremal (deterministic) systems on the 2-sphere are shown numerically to yield interpolatory cubature rules with positive weights.
status_evidence.claim: Positivity of interpolation weights is established for deterministic extremal systems, leaving the random case open.
